title: Harden lifecycle recovery and Python type checks
summary: Hardened lifecycle recovery so failed or interrupted auto-resume remains durably unsafe across backend restarts, and resolved focused Python lint/type issues.
reason: A recovery marker was written but ignored by status checks, allowing a replacement lease after recovery failure or interruption.
behavior_before: A recovery artifact was ignored after the active lease was removed, so a failed or interrupted automatic recovery became idle on restart and allowed replacement work.
behavior_after: A durable recovery-pending record blocks ordinary leases and close readiness; only the server-generated recovery command may acquire one replacement lease, and unsuccessful recovery becomes indeterminate.
manual_validation: Focused pytest lifecycle, API, publish, config, and stage suite - 147 passed, 433 subtests passed
rollback_plan: Revert this packet's source and test changes together; doing so restores the prior automatic-recovery behavior and its weaker restart safety posture.
notes:
Persist recovery-pending lifecycle evidence and fail closed across backend restarts.
Durably block failed automatic recovery attempts.
Cover recovery-pending restart and recovery command lease behavior.
Cover failed automatic recovery durable block.
Resolve pending-publish DTO type annotation and unused imports.
Remove unused configuration-key import.
Use direct resolved local-base access after existence check.
Make dynamic lease binding explicit and release lock safely.
Type dynamic lifecycle lease attachment on subprocess handles.
Remove unused local API route-error import identified by Ruff.
Narrow dry-run optional mapping and collection types for static checking.
Make worker configuration keys visible to static type checking through the compatibility aggregate.
Normalize dynamic network configuration values before typed parsing.
Refresh generated summary for this change.
